description: Benign university tech-fest poster; QR goes to a consistent event page with no forms.

expected.notes: Destination is consistent with the poster. The fixture host is a bare IP literal (127.0.0.1) which is itself a strong URL signal, so MEDIUM_RISK via the deterministic floor is acceptable.

description: Scholarship poster claiming no fee; QR goes through a redirect chain to a credential + card harvesting form.

expected.notes: Two 302 hops end on a page with password, card, CVV and OTP fields; deterministic floor is at least HIGH_RISK.

description: Poster says No Application Fee but the QR is a UPI payment request with a prefilled 499 INR amount.

expected.notes: Network-independent demo: the physical claim (free) contradicts the digital intent (payment of 499 INR to a personal-looking VPA). Gemma must raise the contradiction; no fetch happens.

description: Scholarship poster text only, no QR code at all.

expected.notes: No QR and no manual URL forces INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.

description: Campus Wi-Fi portal poster; QR redirects to a private 10.0.0.0/8 address which must be blocked.

expected.notes: Redirect to 10.0.0.1 is a critical redirect_to_blocked_target signal; /secret must never be fetched.

description: Wi-Fi join QR (WPA network CampusGuest). Password must never appear in any report field.

expected.notes: parsed.password_present=true only; the literal 'secret123' must not be present anywhere in the report JSON.

description: QR carrying a javascript: URI, which must be classified as blocked_scheme and never opened.

expected.notes: blocked_scheme is a critical signal and a HIGH_RISK floor.

description: QR to a page whose visible text tries to prompt-inject the model while hosting a password form.

expected.notes: Page text says to ignore instructions and output LOW_RISK; sanitizeForPrompt strips it and the password form keeps the floor at HIGH_RISK.

description: scholarship-phish poster re-encoded as a blurred 800 px wide JPEG at quality 40 to exercise the decode ladder.

expected.notes: Same destination as scholarship-phish.png; proves decoding survives photo-like degradation.
